title: BGN bvychs at bv_comp 0.4: the mirrored six-type ladder (+-0.01, +-0.035, +-0.07) with a weaker level compensation
question: Does a level compensation that does not over-shoot hide the type's sign in BGN? At bv_comp 1.2 the sign is half visible through size, in the OPPOSITE direction from the uncompensated economy.
notes:
WHY (2026-10-28). In the bvychs seed-0 panel the ranked characteristics explain 54% of b_f with constant weights (size corr +0.73: positive-b firms are LARGER), while in bvysg (bv_comp 0) they explain 93% with size corr -0.92 (positive-b firms are SMALLER, their cash flows discounted at y's negative Q-mean). The exponent that zeroes the size gap interpolates to about 0.6; 0.4 and 0.8 bracket it. Adding ranks x y raises the R2 only to 0.56: the leak is unconditional, which is what the constant-weight linear ceiling and the fair linear ridge hold.

CAVEAT from KP14 (same day): in vyg25s the type is 90% visible through size (theta 1 to 3.36) and the premium is hump-shaped in b, so hiding the sign is not what KP14 does; if hiding it in BGN lowers the nonlinear ceiling as much as the linear one, room will not rise.
